title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-28
notes:
West leads the ♣10 against 6♠. West's lead is won in the closed hand. If trumps are 2-1, the contract will basically depend on either the heart finesse or the diamond finesse working.

If the defense has a trump trick, it appears at first glance that both the heart finesse and the diamond finesse are required. Depending on which defender has a trump trick, only one finesse is actually necessary.

If, for example, South cashes the ♠A and East discards, only the diamond finesse is needed. South should finesse the ♦Q and cash the ♦A. The ♠K is played next. South should then play clubs. If West refuses to ruff in, he is put on lead with his trump trick. West must either lead a heart into South's tenace or a diamond conceding a ruff and discard.

If West discards when the ♠A is cashed, only the heart finesse is required. A second trump is played to the ♠K and the heart finesse is taken. The ♥A is cashed and the clubs are run. East is eventually endplayed with his trump trick. He must either lead a diamond into dummy's tenace or a heart conceding a ruff and discard.
